concurrency_note: The static rules read source; the walk times sequential requests, first load then warm. Concurrent sweeps are the product's concern (one per site) and were not exercised.

authority_boundary.proves: On Go services: a persistence write reachable on a GET handler's request path, a list query with no window, and a store read inside a loop over a result set are reported at file:line with the handler and call chain. A write in an unjoined goroutine is not. Build output is never read and declarations are never counted as writes. The walk fails a GET operation whose first or warm load is over its latency budget.
authority_boundary.artifact: scripts/check_perf.py static/walk/self-test, also run by scripts/saas_gate.py's performance category; fixtures tests/fixtures/perf_gate/{inline_sweep,background_sweep}; a real shipped staff booking service (private repo) at main and with the #434 fix reverted
assumptions: Go only; other stacks are inapplicable, not pass
the call graph is by name, so an interface call reaches every same-named method that takes a context; this over-reaches rather than misses

no flow-sensitivity: a branch made POST-only by an earlier compound condition still reads as GET-reachable (1 known false positive on the real repo); method pruning happens only where it is proven (pure method tests, or a conjunct that excludes GET; code after a block only when the block always returns)
unbounded-list checks that a bound exists, not that it is the asked window

the walk ran against the Firestore emulator on a laptop, with a seed shaped from production aggregate counts (555 requests, 645 replica bookings, 34 prior staff decisions, 120 planned automatic confirms for the site); emulator latency is lower than production's, so this walk understates production times
the walk covered the API route of the defect only; no screen was walked from a browser HAR tonight
cache awareness is by annotation only: a function marked `// cw-perf: cached <reason>` is not followed; an unmarked cached read inside a loop is still reported

a chunk loop is recognised by shape (a `for len(V) > 0` loop that re-slices V, or a range over a variable/call from a function named *Queries/*Chunks/*Batches/chunk*/batch*); a chunk loop built any other way still reads as read-in-loop
